title: The teacher under the tree
hookLine: a minister carrying a king's gold meets a teacher under a tree, and never buys the horses
carry: the teacher is the way: gurur upayah
tomorrow: who is the fierce one with the dog at Shiva's door?

cards: The Pandya king of Madurai gives his chief minister a fortune in gold and one job: ride to the coast and buy the finest horses. On the way, at a place called Tirupperunturai, the minister hears chanting.
Under a tree sits a teacher, with students around him, perfectly calm. The minister gets down from his horse. He meant to stop for a moment.
He falls at the teacher's feet instead, the teacher blesses him, and something in him opens. He never buys the horses.

teach.b: The minister became Manikkavasagar, one of the great poet-saints of Tamil Shaivism; the name means the one whose words are gems.

He spent the king's gold on a temple and on Shiva's devotees, and paid for it: the king had him punished, and in the Madurai telling, yesterday's flood and the laborer who took the cane came for his sake.
And the teacher under the tree? Tradition says it was Shiva himself, come as a guru.

teach.h: THE GURU WAS SHIVA. GURUR UPAYAH.
teach.b: Now the Shiva Sutras: gurur upayah. Guru is a teacher. Upaya is a means, the thing that gets you there.

The teacher is the way. This book has said you are consciousness, that small knowing binds, that the self is a dancer who can forget who's dancing. If that's the problem, more information won't fix it.

teach.h: A HABIT OF SEEING, HANDED ON.
teach.b: It's a habit of seeing, and habits change through someone who has seen.
The commentator Kshemaraja reads the line more widely still: the guru is also Shiva's own grace, his power to reveal, working through a person. That's the teaching under a very Hindu habit.
It's why students touch a teacher's feet, why many keep Guru Purnima, a full-moon day for honoring teachers, and why a mantra is traditionally received from a teacher, not copied off a page.

Grace tends to arrive with a face. And the student still walks: Manikkavasagar still had to get down from his horse. So if something matters to you, a chant, a prayer, an instrument, find the person who can hand it over.

how: Students of Kashmir Shaivism learn the Shiva Sutras from a teacher, line by line; many Hindus honor their teachers by touching their feet, and on Guru Purnima, the full-moon day for teachers.

a sutra saying the teacher, and grace through one, is the way
a sutra saying a guru must do the seeing for you

s: tradition says the teacher under the tree was Shiva himself
Shiva came as a guru to the minister who became Manikkavasagar.
the sutra says the teacher does the seeing for the student
the teacher is the means; the student still walks, the way the minister still got down from his horse.
Kshemaraja reads guru only as a human person
he reads it also as Shiva's grace, his power to reveal.

games.q: you've read every line of the Shiva Sutras and still see through the keyhole. what does today's sutra name as the means?
o: a teacher, and the grace that works through one.
games.why: gurur upayah: the teacher is the way. a habit of seeing changes with help from someone who has seen.

practice: Do what many Hindus do for a teacher. Bring to mind someone who showed you a way: a parent at the stove, a coach, a teacher who stayed after class.
Let their face come, put your palms together, and bow your head toward them, a silent thank-you. If you pray, thank Shiva for the grace that came through them. If you don't, the thank-you is enough.
